subject: PII scrubber gaps fixed (+CC phones, sentence-final phones, USMLE ids); owned MCQs out of the shared index; S15 migration is 0028 and adapts to S20's 0023
body:
S15's 50 MB benchmark (real LLMGateway + fake provider clients + PrivacyDirectory) and the model_eval harness found three gaps in `naadi_api/llm_privacy.py` generic scrubbing. Fixed on my branch (claim 20261117T052410), landing with S15:
1. `+91 98765 43210` (country code + two groups, the usual Indian mobile format) was not matched by `_PHONE` (it needed 2-5 groups before the last). With a `+` prefix one group is now enough; without one the old rule stays (>= 10 digits still required by `_phone_sub`).
2. A number that ends a sentence (`... 43210.`) never matched: the trailing lookahead `(?![\w.])` refused any full stop. Now only `.<digit>` (a decimal) stops a match.
3. The hyphenated USMLE/ECFMG id `5-382-904-1` was not in `_DOC_ID`; added `\d-\d{3}-\d{3}-\d`.
Regression cases added to tests/agent/test_llm_unit.py::test_identifiers_are_still_scrubbed (lab values like `Na 140. K 4.1`, `BP 120/80`, `grade 3-4`, ranges stay untouched; all 91 llm unit tests green). seg04-agents: FYI for your file; tell me if you want a different shape.

Also on S15's branch (S07's loader, one line): `embeddings/sources.py question_docs` now requires `q.owner_user_id is null`: a student's own MCQs (S15 private questions) must never enter the shared index.

seg20-media: your 0023 already added `media_assets.owner_user_id` + `user-upload` source, so my migration (now **0028**, down 0024) does not add the column again; it keeps your read rule (approved + owner) but splits it per role (anon: shared approved only) and adds CHECK `media_assets_owned_private_source`: an owned row's `source_id` must be `user-upload` or `user-provided` (your Anki media already satisfy it). S15's own figures are inserted `approved` + owned, like yours. `user-provided` (allow_ai_ingest true, for the owner's own retrieval of private chapters) stays separate from your `user-upload` (allow_ai_ingest false). Correction to my earlier note: the built-in `flashcards` placement now scores 0.97 when the classifier says flashcard_deck or input is anki, so give `anki_deck` 0.99.
